exchanges.question: Accident year loss ratio improved from Q2 2025 unlike many other commercial insurers. What drove that improvement—was it lower non-cat property losses, changes in loss picks, or other factors?
exchanges.answer: Losses came in below expectations as they have for several quarters, reflecting normal variability and business mix. Loss ratio is composite of a dozen statutory lines. Reserves are as conservative as company history. On commissions: second quarter provides good indication of forward trajectory; slight uptick in commission rate expected going forward; AI activities may provide efficiency gains on operating side; second quarter expense ratio should be good measure going forward.

exchanges.question: Given E&S casualty softening and GWP up only 3% versus 4% in Q1, how much are ROEs compressing given your mid-to-high single digit loss trend views? How are you thinking about broker commissions going forward?
exchanges.answer: Management ROE target is 20% or greater; most product lines running ahead of that; company annualized 24.4% for quarter. On commissions: brokers critical to success and seeking to maximize economics; tension between wholesalers and retail clients on commission split; soft market rate declines pressure all parties. Kinsale offers best customer service in industry with strongest quote ratio and response time, plus broadest risk appetite. Outside Commercial Property, business growing well.

exchanges.question: Does Kinsale view Q2 as property market trough given larger players withdrawing? Can property pricing become less negative in 2027? When can Kinsale return to larger shared placements?
exchanges.answer: No visibility into 2027 direction; pressure persists from MGAs in London and traditional markets in shared layered deals. Role is maintaining tactical pricing to meet return thresholds; shrinking division if necessary. On acceleration to 3.7% growth ex-Commercial Property: competition in long-tail lines and construction creating pricing pressure; pockets of opportunity exist. Some flow returning to admitted market but not pervasive.

exchanges.question: How much of the increase in inbound accounts comes from broker engagement versus competitive pricing? What is current view on social inflation and casualty loss trend landscape?
exchanges.answer: Increase in inbound accounts from both broker engagement and pricing; idle broker initiative reengaging brokers, hit ratios staying roughly same. Confidence in business model despite slower growth in Commercial Property. Casualty loss cost trends mid-single digits varying by line; company less exposed to social inflation due to smaller accounts and lower limits; short tail lines performing especially well. Company being conservative releasing IBNR in longer tail occurrence business.

exchanges.question: What granularity on property pricing Q2 versus Q1? When can property pricing stabilize? Given mix shift from property to casualty, should accident year loss ratio drift up or is current level sustainable?
exchanges.answer: Eventually reach equilibrium; catastrophe losses intermittent and unpredictable but do happen; disciplined pricing and risk management protocol essential. Specialized property areas like Agribusiness seeing growth; small business property more stable than large shared deals; some competition in Inland Marine; people reaching floor on property pricing with pressure from London. Accident year loss ratio hard to predict; could drift up; losses coming below expectations; feel good about loss ratio bookings and very good about IBNR reserve conservatism as positive for future performance.

exchanges.question: How have new products and enhancements contributed to growth, and what is potential uplift going forward?
exchanges.answer: Never want to jump in feet first and grow like weed; always crawl, walk, run pace. New products creating growth, driving submissions and new premium. Growth will be slow, ramping up as market turns.
